BURHAN:v3p143/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p143/r3.speaker: الكسائي
BURHAN:v3p143/r3.claim: Al-Kisa’i allows an unexpressed agent whenever context identifies it: the soul reaches the collarbones, the sun disappears, punishment descends, or a messenger comes to Solomon.
BURHAN:v3p143/r3.anchor: وجوز الكسائي حذفه مطلقا إذا ما وجد ما يدل عليه

BURHAN:v3p143/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p143/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p143/r4.claim: The author’s correction is that the agent in these examples is implicit, not deleted; he distinguishes the two grammatical analyses.
BURHAN:v3p143/r4.anchor: والحق أنه في المذكورات مضمر لا محذوف وقد سبق الفرق بينهما

ITQAN:v2p566/r32.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r32.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p566/r32.claim: التراقي is the plural of ترقوة, with an open first vowel.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r12.claim: Kalla rebukes preferring this world to the next and reminds hearers of death, which ends the immediate life; ‘when it reaches’ refers to the soul implied by context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p350/r12.anchor: كلا: ردع عن إيثار الدنيا على الآخرة وتذكير لهم بما يؤولون إليه من الموت

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p221/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p221/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p221/r2.claim: The feminine pronoun in balaghat refers to the soul although it was not mentioned; this omission, like other missing subjects, matches the surah's haste.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p221/r2.anchor: والضمير في {بَلَغَتِ} للنفس وإن لم يَجْرِ لها ذِكْرٌ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r3.claim: Haste appears through omitted elements: the oath's answer, the governing verb of qadirin, the antecedent of the tongue pronoun, and the unstated subject of balaghat.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r3.anchor: فمن مراعاة جانب العجلة: 1- حذف جواب القسم الذي افتتحت به السورة وهو {لاَ أُقْسِمُ}

ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r1.claim: The scene turns from the cosmic end and afterlife outcomes to death, the individual’s final crisis and first gate into the next life; worldly attachment begins to break its victims already in this world.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r1.anchor: hayât-ı dünyanın sonu ve âhiretin ilk kapısı ve ferdin kıyameti demek olan ölüm ve sekerât-ı mevt hâli tasvir olunarak

ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r2.claim: “Kallā idhā” warns those who love the immediate world and begins the depiction of death.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r2.anchor: âcileye mahabbetle âhireti terkten tahzir ve mevt hâlini tasvirdir.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r3.claim: The pronoun in “when it reaches the collarbones” may refer to the soul that loves the world or, by contextual association, to the spirit.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r3.anchor: Zamiri, dünyaya mahabbet eden nefse yahut o karîne ile rûha râci‘dir.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r4.claim: “Tarāqī” is the plural of “tarquwa,” the collarbones at the base of the neck toward the arms.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r4.anchor: “Turkuve”nin cem‘idir ki boyunun dibinden kollara doğru olan köprücük kemiklerine denir.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r11.claim: For lovers of this world, death is painful and endless separation and exile; for those devoted to the afterlife, the same moment brings release and joyful union.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r11.anchor: bu lahza dünya mahabbetine sargın rûhlar için böyle elîm bir firak, nihâyetsiz bir hicran

NAHHAS:v5p92/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r4.claim: Kalla can mean “indeed” and can serve as a subject in this construction.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r4.anchor: تكون بمعنى حقا وتكون مبتدأ على هذا ههنا

NAHHAS:v5p92/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r5.speaker: محمد بن جرير
NAHHAS:v5p92/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir says the pause belongs at kalla: the claim being refuted is that polytheists will not be requited for their shirk and disobedience.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r5.anchor: وزعم محمد بن جرير أن التمام ههنا كلا وأن المعنى ليس الأمر كما يقول المشركون من أنهم لا يجازون على شركهم ومعصيتهم

NAHHAS:v5p92/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r6.claim: The governor of idha may be basira or balaghat; if balaghat governs it, the answer occurs later in the passage.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r6.anchor: ( إذا بلغت التراقي ) يكون العامل في إذا باسرة أو بلغت فإذا كان العامل فيها بلغت كان الجواب فيما بعد

SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r1.claim: Al-tarāqī is the object of بلغت; its unexpressed subject is the soul, though the soul has not been mentioned, as in Ḥātim’s verse where حشرجت has an implicit feminine subject.
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r1.anchor: مفعول " بلغت " ، والفاعل مضمر [يعود] على النفس، وإن لم يجر لها ذكر، كقول حاتم:

SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r2.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r2.claim: An alternative reading of Ḥātim’s line infers the soul from its encompassing content, ‘wealth’; likewise, mentioning the human here indicates the soul.
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r2.anchor: وقيل في البيت: إن الدال على النفس ذكر جملة ما اشتمل عليها، وهو الغنى، فكذلك هنا ذكر الإنسان دال على النفس.

SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r3.claim: The plural is from tarquwah, underlyingly تراقو; its wāw becomes yāʾ because the preceding consonant has kasrah. Its pattern is فعلوة, with original tāʾ and augmentative wāw; Abū al-Baqāʾ likewise rejects تفعلة because رقو is unattested.
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r3.anchor: والتراقي: جمع ترقوة، أصلها تراقو، قلبت واوها ياء لانكسار ما قبلها.

SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r4.claim: The Shaykh calls the collarbone one of the chest bones, but al-Samīn says that is not the recognized meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r4.anchor: والترقوة إحدى عظام الصدر، كذا قال الشيخ، والمعروف غير ذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says each person has two collarbones; the dual body-part plural is like describing someone as thick-browed or broad-shouldered.
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ولكل إنسان ترقوتان " فعلى هذا تكون من باب: غليظ الحواجب وعريض المناكب

SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r6.claim: The tarāqī are the site of the death rattle; an anonymous poem witnesses the idiom of people’s souls reaching the collarbones.
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r6.anchor: والتراقي: موضع الحشرجة. قال: 4420 ورب عظيمة دافعت عنها

SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r7.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib defines the collarbone as the bone joining the hollow at the base of the neck to the shoulder.
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r7.anchor: وقال الراغب: " الترقوة عظم وصل ما بين ثغرة النحر والعاتق "

SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defines the collarbones as the bones flanking the hollow at the base of the neck on the right and left.
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " العظام المكتنفة لثغرة النحر عن يمين وشمال "

SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r9.claim: A reading has sukūn on the yāʾ of التراقي, compared with Zayd’s reading أهاليكم; its justification was discussed earlier.
SAMIN-DURR:75:26/r9.anchor: وقرىء " التراقي " بسكون الياء، وهي كقراءة زيد " تطعمون أهاليكم "

ZAJJAJ:v5p253/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p253/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p253/r4.claim: ‘Kallā’ is a rebuke and warning: desist from what leads to punishment.
ZAJJAJ:v5p253/r4.anchor: (كلا) ردع وتنبيه، ومعناه ارتدعوا عما يؤدي إلى العذاب.

ZAJJAJ:v5p253/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p253/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p253/r5.claim: The verse reminds people of the first hardship of the Hereafter, when the soul reaches the collarbones.
ZAJJAJ:v5p253/r5.anchor: ذكرهم الله بصعوبة أول أيام الآخرة عند بلوغ النفس الترقوة.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r5.speaker: أبو بكر بن مجاهد
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r5.claim: Ibn Mujāhid recited the sūra in dawn prayer, pausing on the yāʾ of التراقي; the following yāʾ in من مني يمنى makes that letter clear.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r5.anchor: وكان أبو بكر بن مجاهد رضي الله عنه يقرأ بهذه السورة في صلاة الصبح فيعتمد الوقف على الياء من قوله

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r7.claim: After rebuking love of the immediate life and neglect of the afterlife, the passage reinforces the warning by turning to death and the good or evil outcome of those preferences.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r7.anchor: ولما ردع سبحانه عن حب العاجلة وترك الآخرة عقب ذلك بما يتضمن تأكيد هذا الردع مما يصير إلى حسن عاقبة حب الآخرة وسوء مغبة العاجلة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes preferring the immediate life over the afterlife and warns people to attend to the approaching death that ends their connection to worldly pleasures.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r1.anchor: ردع عن إيثار العاجلة على الآخرة كأنه قيل ارتدعوا عن ذلك وتنبهوا لما بين أيديكم من الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r2.claim: The feminine subject of balaghat is omitted and understood as the soul or spirit from context; Arabic can simply say it ‘reached’ without naming it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r2.anchor: أي النفس أو الروح الدالعلى سياق الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r3.claim: The tarāqī are the upper chest bones bordering the hollow of the throat on the right and left; Arabic usage may say that the soul has reached them.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r3.anchor: أي أعالي الصدر وهي العظام المكتنفة ثغرة النحر عن يمين وشمال جمع ترقوة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r4.speaker: حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r4.claim: Ḥātim’s verse about wealth being useless when a person is gathered and the chest constricts exemplifies omitting the soul as subject of ‘reaching.’
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r4.anchor: كما في قول حاتم أماوي ما يغنى الثراء عن الفتى إذا حشر جت يوما وضاق بها الصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r5.claim: The expression resembles Arabs saying ‘it sent’ to mean that rain came, though they seldom explicitly say ‘the sky sent.’
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r5.anchor: ونحو قول العرب أرسلت يريدون جاء المطر ولا تكاد تسمعهم يقولون أرسلت السماء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r6.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r6.claim: A line by Durayd ibn al-Ṣimma describes people’s souls reaching the collarbones, attesting to the expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p146#4/r6.anchor: وأنشدوا لدريد بن الصمة ورب عظيمة رافعت عنهم وقد بلغت نفوسهم التراقي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p285/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p285/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p285/r6.claim: The unexpressed subject of reaching the collarbones is the soul, which rattles there at death; this phrase idiomatically means nearing death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p285/r6.anchor: كلا إذا بلغت} يعني النفس، كناية عن غير مذكور {التراقي} فحشرج بها عند الموت،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p285/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p285/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p285/r7.claim: Tarāqī is the plural of tarquwa, the bones between the hollow of the throat and the shoulder.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p285/r7.anchor: و"التراقي" جمع الترقوة، وهي العظام بين ثغرة النحر والعاتق،

DURR-FULL:v8p360/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p360/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p360/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the collarbones in the verse with the throat.
DURR-FULL:v8p360/r10.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه في قوله: {إذا بلغت التراقي} قال: الحلقوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r1.speaker: المغيرة بن شعبة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r1.claim: Al-Mughira reports the saying that each person’s own Resurrection is his death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r1.anchor: وعن المغيرة بن شعبة يقولون : القيامة القيامة ، وإنما قيامة أحدهم موته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r2.speaker: علقمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r2.claim: Alqama attended a funeral and, after the burial, said that this person’s Resurrection had begun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r2.anchor: وعن علقمة أنه حضر جنازة فلما دفن قال : ( أما هذا فقد قامت قيامته )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r3.claim: The death throes are the final state of earthly life, after which the soul passes directly into God’s disposal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r3.anchor: فحالة الاحتضار هي آخر أحوال الحياة الدنيا يعقبها مصير الروح إلى تصرف الله تعالى مباشرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r4.claim: The warning calls people to stop preferring worldly life and attend to imminent death, when the present life ends and the next begins.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r4.anchor: وهو ردع عن إيثار الدنيا على الآخرة كأنه قيل : ارتدعوا وتنبهوا على ما بين أيديكم من الموت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r5.claim: This is a fresh warning about the preference for worldly life implied in 75:20, not merely a repetition of that earlier rebuke.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r5.anchor: فليس مؤكدا للردع الذي في قوله : { كلا بل تحبون العاجلة } ( القيامة : 20 ) بل هو ردع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r6.claim: “When it reaches the collarbones” attaches to the implied predicate “the journey is to your Lord.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r6.anchor: و { إذا بلغت التراقي } متعلق بالكون الذي يقدر في الخبر وهو قوله : { إلى ربك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r7.claim: “The journey is to your Lord” explains the warning and brings near a refutation of the deniers’ question about when Resurrection will come (75:6).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r7.anchor: وجملة { إلى ربك يومئذ المساق } بيان للردع وتقريب لإبطال الاستبعاد المحكي عن منكري البعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r9.claim: The feminine subject of “reaches” is unexpressed but understood as the soul; Hatim al-Taʾi’s line similarly omits “the soul,” and Arabs use “I sent” for the sky sending rain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r9.anchor: ومثله قول حاتم الطائي : أماوي ما يغني الثراء عن الفتى إذا حشرجت يوما وضاق بها الصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r10.claim: The plural “breaths” is from nafas with an open fāʾ, which Ibn ʿĀshūr considers the more factually apt form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p357/r10.anchor: والأنفاس : جمع نفس ، بفتح الفاء ، وهو أنسب بالحقائق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r1.claim: Tarāqī is the plural of tarquwa, the hollow at the base of the neck; every person has two, one on each side.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r1.anchor: و { التراقي } : جمع ترقوة ( بفتح الفوقية وسكون الراء وضم القاف وفتح الواو مخففة وهاء تأنيث )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r2.claim: The plural is used for the dual to lighten the expression and avoid the heaviness of the dual form; 66:4 similarly uses “your hearts.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r2.anchor: فالجمع هنا مستعمل في التثنية لقصد تخفيف اللفظ وقد أمن اللبس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r3.claim: The soul has reached the throat, where its final breaths emerge: the last stage of dying, as in 56:83.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r3.anchor: ومعنى بلغت التراقي } : أن الروح بلغت الحنجرة حيث تخرج الأنفاس الأخيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r4.claim: The definite article in “the collarbones” stands in for the omitted possessor: the soul reaches the person’s collarbones, as with “the journey.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p358/r4.anchor: واللام في { التراقي } مثل اللام في المساق فيقال : هي عوض عن المضاف إليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says kalla is a rebuke and warning, telling them to desist from what leads to punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج كلا ردع وتنبيه المعنى ارتدعوا عما يؤدي إلى العذاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r2.claim: Another reported view says kalla means that the disbeliever does not believe this.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r2.anchor: وقال غيره معنى كلا لا يؤمن الكافر بهذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r3.claim: The unstated subject of reached is the soul; the phrase leaves it unmentioned.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r3.anchor: إذا بلغت يعني النفس وهذه كناية عن غير مذكور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r4.claim: The taraqi are the bones surrounding the hollow at the top of the chest on both sides; one bone is a tarquwa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r4.anchor: والتراقي العظام المكتنفة لنقرة النحر عن يمين وشمال وواحدة التراقي ترقوة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r5.claim: Saying that the soul reaches the collarbones is an idiom for nearing death.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p423#3/r5.anchor: ويكنى ببلوغ النفس التراقي عن الإشفاء على الموت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r1.claim: The passage describes the terrors of dying.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن حالة الاحتضار وما عنده من الأهوال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r2.claim: If kalla is rebuke, it means a person will no longer deny what was foretold once it becomes visible.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r2.anchor: إن جعلنا {كلا} رداعة فمعناها: لست يا ابن آدم تكذب هناك بما أخبرت به، بل صار ذلك عندك عيانا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r3.claim: If kalla means “truly,” the soul leaves the body and reaches the collarbones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r3.anchor: وإن جعلناها بمعنى (حقا) فظاهر، أي: حقا إذا بلغت التراقي، أي: انتزعت روحك من جسدك وبلغت تراقيك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r4.claim: Taraqi is plural of tarquwa, the bones between the hollow at the neck and the shoulder.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r4.anchor: والتراقي: جمع ترقوة، وهي العظام التي بين ثغرة النحر والعاتق،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r5.claim: The scene connects to the passage where the soul reaches the throat and onlookers watch but cannot see.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p281#2/r5.anchor: كقوله: {فلولا إذا بلغت الحلقوم وأنتم حينئذ تنظرون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes preferring worldly life to the Hereafter and calls people to notice death, when present life ends and everlasting afterlife begins.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r1.anchor: ردع عن إيثار الدنيا على الآخرة ، كأنه قيل : ارتدعوا عن ذلك ، وتنبهوا على ما بين أيديكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r2.claim: The unexpressed subject of ‘reaches’ is the soul; the surrounding discourse makes it clear, just as Arabic may say ‘it rained’ without naming the sky.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r2.anchor: والضمير في { بلغت } للنفس وإن لم يجر لها ذكر ، لأن الكلام الذي وقعت فيه يدل عليها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r3.claim: Ḥātim’s verse illustrates the soul’s death rattle and constricted chest; the Arabs likewise say ‘I sent’ meaning that rain came, without mentioning the sky.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r3.anchor: كما قال حاتم : أماوي ما يغني الثراء عن الفتى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r4.claim: Al-tarāqī are the bones on either side enclosing the hollow at the base of the neck.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r4.anchor: { التراقي } العظام المكتنفة لثغرة النحر عن يمين وشمال . ذكرهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r5.claim: The verse evokes death’s severity as the soul reaches the collarbones and its departure nears, the first stage of the Hereafter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664/r5.anchor: ذكرهم صعوبة الموت الذي هو أول مراحل الآخرة حين تبلغ الروح التراقي ودنا زهوقها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes preferring this world over the afterlife and tells people to desist.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ كلا ﴾ ردع عن ايثار الدنيا على الآخرة كأنه قبل ارتدعوا عن ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r2.claim: He urges preparation for imminent death: the present life ends then, and people pass to an everlasting afterlife.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r2.anchor: الموت الذي عنده تنقطع العاجلة عنكم وتنتقلون إلى لآجلة التي تبقون فيها مخلدين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r3.claim: The subject that reaches the collarbones is the soul, inferred from the verse despite lacking an earlier mention.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r3.anchor: أي الروح وجاز وإن لم يجر لها ذكر لان الآية تدل عليها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r4.claim: Al-tarāqī are the bones flanking the hollow at the throat, the plural of tarquwah.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#3/r4.anchor: العظام المكتنفة لثغرة النحر عن يمين وشمال جمع ترقوة

BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r14.claim: The unexpressed feminine subject of balaghat is the soul, inferred from context though not previously mentioned.
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r14.anchor: الضمير للنفس وإن لم يجر لها ذكر لأن الكلام الذي وقعت فيه يدل عليها

BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r15.claim: The tarāqī are bones around the hollow at the base of the neck on either side; reaching them marks the death rattle.
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r15.anchor: وهي العظام المكتنفة لثغرة النحر عن يمين وشمال فإذا بلغت إليها يكون وقت الغرغرة

BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r16.claim: At this point the rational soul, the human spirit, reaches the collarbones and death is imminent.
BURSEVI:v10p195#2/r16.anchor: إذا بلغت النفس الناطقة وهي الروح الإنساني أالي الصر وهي العظام

QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r1.claim: Kalla rebukes and warns: it is far-fetched that a disbeliever would believe in Resurrection; the passage begins a clause about the soul reaching the collarbones.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r1.anchor: «كلا» ردع وزجر أي بعيد أن يؤمن الكافر بيوم القيامة ثم استأنف فقال: { إذا بلغت التراقي

QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r2.claim: The understood subject is the soul or spirit, though it was not previously named, as in cited verses about the sun disappearing and the soul reaching the throat.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r2.anchor: أي بلغت النفس أو الروح التراقي فأخبر عما لم يجر له ذكر، لعلم المخاطب به كقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r3.claim: Another view takes kalla to mean ‘truly’: the journey is to God when the soul reaches the collarbones.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r3.anchor: وقيل: «كلا» معناه حقا أي حقا أن المساق إلى الله «إذا بلغت التراقي»

QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas specifies that it is the disbeliever's soul that reaches the collarbones.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r4.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول: إذا بلغت نفس الكافر التراقي.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r5.claim: Taraqi is the plural of tarquwa, the bones enclosing the hollow at the base of the throat, at the upper chest where death rattle occurs.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r5.anchor: والتراقي جمع ترقوة وهي العظام المكتنفة لنقرة النحر، وهو مقدم الحلق من أعلى الصدر، موضع الحشرجة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r6.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r6.claim: Duraid ibn al-Simma uses reaching the collarbones as an idiom for nearing death.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r6.anchor:
قال دريد بن الصمة.
ورب عظيمة دافعت

QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r7.claim: The idiom evokes nearing death to remind people of the severity of the moment as death descends.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:26-28/r7.anchor: وقد يكنى عن الإشفاء على الموت ببلوغ النفس التراقي، والمقصود تذكيرهم شدة الحال عند نزول الموت.

RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes kalla as a rebuke against preferring worldly life: the afterlife's fates dwarf the world, and death ends the temporary life before the eternal one.
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج : كلا ردع عن إيثار الدنيا على الآخرة ، كأنه قيل : لما عرفتم صفة سعادة السعداء

RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r2.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r2.claim: Others read kalla as “indeed”: when death arrives, worldly life necessarily ends and one tastes death's bitterness.
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون : { كلا } أي حقا إذا بلغت التراقي كان كذا وكذا

RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r3.claim: Muqatil says the unbeliever denies the resurrection but cannot deny that death and its pains must come.
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل : { كلا } أي لا يؤمن الكافر بما ذكر من أمر القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r4.claim: The omitted subject of “reaches the collarbones” is the soul or spirit, understood by the audience; tarāqī is the paired collarbones between the throat hollow and shoulders.
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r4.anchor: المسألة الأولى : المراد إذا بلغت النفس أو الروح أخبر عما لم يجر له ذكر

RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r5.claim: The soul reaching the collarbones is a euphemism for nearing death, as in Duraid ibn al-Simma's verse about lives reaching the collarbones.
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r5.anchor: واعلم أنه يكنى ببلوغ النفس التراقي عن القرب من الموت ، ومنه قول دريد بن الصمة

RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r6.claim: The same nearness-to-death expression appears in the Qur'an as reaching the throat.
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r6.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { وبلغت * الحلقوم } ( الأحزاب : 10 )

RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r7.claim: A critic argues that the soul reaches the collarbones only after leaving the heart, which would mean death already occurred, although the passage still describes signs of life.
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r7.anchor: المسألة الثالثة : قال بعض الطاعنين : إن النفس إنما تصل إلى التراقي بعد مفارقتها

RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r8.claim: Al-Razi answers that the phrase means nearing that state, not fully reaching it, so it does not imply that life continues after death.
RAZI-FULL:v30p203#2/r8.anchor: والجواب : المراد من قوله : { حتى إذا * بلغت التراقي } أي إذا حصل القرب

STUDYQURAN:75:26/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:26/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:26/r1.claim: Kallā is emphatic and negative here as “Nay,” but may also be read affirmatively as “truly” or “indeed.”
STUDYQURAN:75:26/r1.anchor: Nay translates the emphatic particle kallā, which can also be read in the affirmative, meaning “truly” or “indeed.”

STUDYQURAN:75:26/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:26/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:26/r2.claim: The reaching of the collarbones refers to the soul's moment of death, as it is about to leave the body.
STUDYQURAN:75:26/r2.anchor: It refers to the soul, and its reaching the collarbones refers to the moment of death when the soul is about to leave the body

STUDYQURAN:75:26/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:26/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:75:26/r3.claim: IK says the negative reading means death discloses truth beyond denial, while the affirmative reading means the soul's departure is certain.
STUDYQURAN:75:26/r3.anchor: When kallā is read in the affirmative, the verse indicates there is no doubt that the soul will leave the body (IK).

TABRISI:75:26-28/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:26-28/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:26-28/r2.claim: Al-tarāqī is the plural of tarquwa, the upper front of the chest; breath rises there at death, vapor ascends from within, and the death rattle occurs there, as Dhū al-Rumma's verse illustrates.
TABRISI:75:26-28/r2.anchor: التراقي جمع الترقوة وهو مقدم الحلق من أعلى الصدر

TABRISI:75:26-28/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:26-28/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:26-28/r13.claim: Here kallā means that the disbeliever does not believe this.

TABRISI:75:26-28/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:26-28/r14.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:75:26-28/r14.claim: An alternative takes kallā as an emphatic affirmation: truly.
TABRISI:75:26-28/r14.anchor: وقيل: معناه حقا { إذا بلغت } النفس أو الروح

TABRISI:75:26-28/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:26-28/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:26-28/r15.claim: The omitted subject of balaghat is the soul or spirit; the wording follows context, like omitting the earth in the phrase about what remains on its back (35:45).
TABRISI:75:26-28/r15.anchor: النفس أو الروح ولم يذكره لدلالة الكلام عليه كما قال ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة

TABRISI:75:26-28/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:26-28/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:26-28/r16.claim: The bones surrounding the throat stand for the body's nearing death.
TABRISI:75:26-28/r16.anchor: أي العظام المكتنفة بالحلق وكنى بذلك عن الإشفاء على الموت

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#8/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#8/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#8/r1.claim: What reaches the collarbones is the soul, now situated between the person's collarbones.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#8/r1.anchor: {كلا إذا بلغت التراقي} يعني: النفس؛ أي صارت النفس بين تراقيه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq calls kalla a rebuke and warning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: هو ردع وتنبيه (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r2.claim: Muqatil says the disbeliever does not believe the preceding account of resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: (كلا) أي لا يؤمن الكافر بما ذكر من أمر القيامة (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r3.claim: When the soul or spirit reaches the collarbones, the referent is omitted because the audience understands it, as with the sun disappearing from view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r3.anchor: يعني: بلغت النفس أو الروح، أخبر عما لم يجر له ذكر لعلم المخاطب بذلك، كقوله تعالى: {حتى توارت بالحجاب}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r4.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad and other commentators say the soul reaches the collarbones; tarāqī is the plural of tarquwa, like ʿarquwa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r4.anchor: قاله المبرد (¬4)، وغيره (¬5) (¬6)، وكلهم (¬7) قالوا: بلغت النفس التراقي. وهي جمع ترقوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r5.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r5.claim: Al-Layth defines a tarquwa as a bone joining the hollow of the throat to the shoulder on either side.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r5.anchor: قال الليث: وهي عظم وصل بين ثغرة النحر والعاتق من الجانبين (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r6.claim: The soul’s reaching the collarbones is a euphemism for nearing death, as Duraid ibn al-Simma’s verse shows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r6.anchor: ويكنى ببلوغ النفس التراقي عن الإشفاء على الموت، ومنه قول دريد بن الصمة: ورب عظيمة دافعت عنها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r7.claim: Muqatil says the soul has reached the throat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني بلغت النفس الحلقوم (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God reminds people of the first hardship of the afterlife when the soul reaches the collarbone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p514/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج: ذكرهم الله صعوبة أول أيام الآخرة عند بلوغ النفس الترقوة

DAMGHANI:v1p86/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p86/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p86/r4.claim: الترائب means the chest ribs, which Damghani equates with the collarbones or ترَاقي.
DAMGHANI:v1p86/r4.anchor: الثالث : الترائب الضلوع من الصدر . قوله تعالى في سورة الطارق

TABATABAI:75:24-30/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r5.claim: The warning rebukes preference for the immediate: death arrives and they are driven to their Lord; the implied subject is the soul, as in 56:83.
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r5.anchor: ردع عن حبهم العاجلة وإيثارها على الآخرة كأنه قيل ارتدعوا عن ذلك فليس يدوم عليكم وسينزل عليكم الموت

TABATABAI:75:24-30/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r6.claim: The omitted subject of ‘reaches’ is the soul, understood from context and the parallel wording in 56:83.
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r6.anchor: وفاعل { بلغت } محذوف يدل عليه السياق

TABATABAI:75:24-30/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r7.claim: The tarāqi are bones surrounding the throat on the right and left; the word is the plural of tarquwa.
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r7.anchor: والتراقي العظام المكتنفة للنحر عن يمين وشمال جمع ترقوة

TABATABAI:75:16-40/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r12.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r12.claim: Al-Qummī says that when the soul reaches the collarbone someone asks who can treat or recite over him; he knows it is separation, and the final journey is to the Lord of the worlds.
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r12.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { كلا إذا بلغت التراقي } قال يعني النفس

TABATABAI:75:16-40/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r13.claim: In al-Kāfī, Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir, answering Jābir, says the dying person asks for a doctor, realizes he is leaving loved ones, and that one leg entwining with the other is the world entwining with the hereafter; the journey is to the Lord of the worlds.
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r13.anchor: إلى جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سألته عن قول الله عز وجل { وقيل من راق وظن أنه الفراق }

TABRISI:75:29-36/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:29-36/r1.claim: A report describes a dying servant grappling with death's pangs while his joints bid one another farewell until the Resurrection.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r1.anchor: أن العبد ليعالج كرب الموت وسكراته

THALABI:v10p88/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p88/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p88/r10.claim: The unexpressed subject is the soul: when it reaches the collarbones, the dying person gasps.
THALABI:v10p88/r10.anchor: كلا إذا بلغت يعني النفس كناية عن غير مذكور التراقي فيحشرج بها عند الموت

THALABI:v10p88/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p88/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p88/r11.claim: The taraqi are the bones bordering the hollow at the base of the neck on both sides.
THALABI:v10p88/r11.anchor: والتراقي: العظام المكتنفة لثغرة النحر عن يمين وشمال

THALABI:v10p88/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p88/r12.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
THALABI:v10p88/r12.claim: Duraid ibn al-Simma's verse uses taraqi for the collarbones reached by the dying person's soul.
THALABI:v10p88/r12.anchor: وقال دريد بن الصمة: ورب عظيمة دافعت عنهم … وقد بلغت نفوسهم التراقي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r8.claim: What reaches the collarbones is the soul.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r8.anchor: { كلا إذا بلغت التراقي } يعني: النفس. بلغت عظام الحلق.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r1.claim: As death approaches and the soul reaches the throat, bystanders ask whether a healer can save the dying person.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r1.anchor: Can boğaza gelip de hasta ölmek üzere olduğunda çevresindekiler, “Bunu ölümden kurtaracak bir şifacı yok mu?” diye sorarak son bir çarenin bulunup bulunmadığını araştırırlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r2.claim: Another interpretation has the angel of death ask whether angels of mercy or angels of punishment will take the soul.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r2.anchor: Bir yoruma göre de ölüm meleği, “Bunun ruhunu rahmet melekleri mi yoksa azap melekleri mi götürecektir?” diye sorarlar.

BURHAN:v4p26/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p26/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p26/r5.claim: In the clauses about reaching the throat or collarbones, the soul is omitted but understood from those body parts.
BURHAN:v4p26/r5.anchor: اضمر النفس لدلالة ذكر الحلقوم والتراقي عليها

ITQAN:v2p547#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r6.claim: A later antecedent may be implied by entailment: the throat and collarbones imply the soul, and the veil implies the sun.
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r6.anchor: أو متأخرا دالا بالإلتزام نحو ﴿ فلولا إذا بلغت الحلقوم ﴾ ﴿ كلا إذا بلغت التراقي ﴾ أضمر الروح أو النفس

FARRA:v3p211/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p211/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p211/r8.claim: At death the soul reaches the collarbones; bystanders ask whether a healer is present, and the dying person knows separation has come.
FARRA:v3p211/r8.anchor: إذا بلغت نفس الرجل عند الموت تراقيه، وقال من حوله: «من راق؟» هل [من ] مداو؟

ASAD-NOTES:75:26/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:26/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:26/r1.claim: As the last breath reaches the throat, people ask whether a wizard can save the dying man.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r3.claim: No one escapes: all must undergo death's agony and, helplessly, begin the journey toward their Lord.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p79/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p79/r3.speaker: Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p79/r3.claim: Farāhī says the unstated antecedent of the pronoun at the soul’s reaching the collarbone is the soul; Arabic permits this omission, illustrated by 56:83 and Hātim al-Ṭā’ī’s verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p79/r3.anchor: my mentor, Im ām Far āhī, has written while explaining these

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p80/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p80/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p80/r1.claim: The pronoun “her” in 35:45 has the suppressed antecedent “earth,” another Qur’anic example of leaving an understood antecedent unmentioned.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p80/r1.anchor: Here one can see that the antecedent of the pronoun

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r2.claim: The rebuke is against preferring worldly life over the afterlife.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r2.anchor: ردع عن إيثار الدنيا على الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r5.claim: The rebuke means that love of the immediate world cannot continue: it will be violently broken at the terror of death.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r5.anchor: أي لا يدوم هذا الحب بل لا بد أن ينقطع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r6.claim: The unspoken subject of “reaches” is the soul, inferred because it is the one that loves the present world.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r6.anchor: ولما كان المحب للدنيا هو النفس

BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r7.claim: The tarāqī are the upper chest bones around the throat on both sides, between the hollow of the neck and the shoulder; their arrival marks death’s choking onset.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r7.anchor: أي عظام أعالي الصدر , جمع ترقوة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r8.claim: Using a plural for the pair may suggest the soul’s desperate movement from the body’s farthest parts into a narrowing space, seeking the nearest exit.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r8.anchor: لعله جمع المثنى إشارة إلى شدة انتشارها بغاية الجهد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r9.speaker: حاتم الطائي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r9.claim: Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī’s verse says wealth cannot help when the dying person chokes and the chest tightens, illustrating the death scene.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253/r9.anchor: قول حاتم الطائي وأشد التئامه مع ما هنا من أمر الروح : أماوي ما يغني الثراء عن الفتى إذا حشرجت يوما وضاق بها الصدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r7.claim: In إذا بلغت التراقي, what reaches the collarbones is the soul.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r7.anchor: كلا إذا بلغت التراقي يعني النفس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p405/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p405/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p405/r7.claim: This is another rebuke to Quraysh, recalling the terrifying and unavoidable death struggle imposed on every creature.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p405/r7.anchor: كلا إذا بلغت زجر آخر لقريش وتذكير لهم بموطن من مواطن الهول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p405/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p405/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p405/r8.claim: Taraqi are the collarbones, aligned with the throats; the plural reflects النفس as a generic class, and the scene describes the death rattle and struggle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p405/r8.anchor: والتراقي ترقوة وهي عظام أعلى الصدر

JISHUMI:v10p7192/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r3.claim: Al-tarāqī are the paired bones around the throat; another description calls them the upper front of the throat, where the soul rises and death rattles occur.
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r3.anchor: التراقي: العظام المكتنفة للحلق يمينا وشمالا، وقيل: مقدم الحلق

JISHUMI:v10p7192/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r4.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r4.claim: The cited line by Durayd ibn al-Ṣimmah uses al-tarāqī for the place the soul reaches at death.
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r4.anchor: فرب عظيمة دافعت عنهم ... وقد بلغت نفوسهم التراقي

JISHUMI:v10p7193/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r3.claim: Kallā may mean truly, or deny what they think and warn that they will learn the truth when the soul reaches the collarbones.
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r3.anchor: قيل: حقا، وقيل: ليس الأمر كما يظنون، ولكن سيعلمون إذا بلغت التراقي

JISHUMI:v10p7193/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r4.claim: The soul reaching the collarbones is expressed by ellipsis: the soul is not named, but the context indicates it.
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r4.anchor: بلغت النفس التراقي كناية عن غير مذكور؛ لأن في الكلام ما يدل عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r1.claim: At death the soul reaches the clavicles, the upper part of the chest.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r1.anchor: يعني بلوغ الروح عند موته إلى التراقي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r2.claim: Tarquwa is the singular form of the plural taraqi, clavicles.

MUQATIL:75:22-33/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r5.claim: The repudiation means they do not believe in what has been said about the Resurrection.
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r5.anchor: { كلا } لا يؤمن بما ذكر في أمر القيامة

MUQATIL:75:22-33/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r6.claim: When the souls reach the collarbones, they have reached the throat.
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r6.anchor: { إذا بلغت } الأنفس { التراقي } [آية: 26] يعني الحلقوم
